Annotate the cell types of a Seurat object in one call

Source: R/scrna-celltype-annotation.R
RunSeuratCellTypeAnnotation.Rd

Runs a cell type annotation tool with RunCellTypeAnnotation() and writes the result into the object with EmbedSeuratCellTypeAnnotation(), so that a Seurat object goes in and an annotated Seurat object comes out. Use the two functions directly instead when the record itself is needed — biopipen's CellTypeAnnotation process keeps it per case to write its cluster2celltype/cell2celltype tables.

Usage

RunSeuratCellTypeAnnotation(
  object,
  tool,
  args = list(),
  ident = NULL,
  case = NULL,
  anno_col = "CellType",
  add_prefix = TRUE,
  set_ident = TRUE,
  merge = FALSE,
  cache = NULL,
  subset = NULL,
  log = NULL
)

Arguments

object

Seurat object

tool

Name of the tool to run, see celltype_annotation_tools(). Case insensitive.

args

Arguments for the tool, as documented in RunCellTypeAnnotation().

ident

The metadata column with the clusters, or "ident" for the identity column. Defaults to the identity column for cluster-based calls.

case

Name of the case the annotation comes from, used as the prefix of the new column names unless add_prefix is FALSE. NULL (default) adds no prefix.

anno_col

Name of the metadata column to store the annotation in.

add_prefix

Whether to prefix the new column names with case.

set_ident

Whether to set the identity of the object to the annotation column.

merge

Whether to merge the clusters annotated with the same cell type. Otherwise a suffix (.1, .2, ...) is added to the cell types.

cache

Directory for conversions and tool scratch files, default tempdir().

subset

An expression to subset the cells to annotate, passed to tidyseurat::filter() on the metadata (the same convention as biopipen's CellTypeAnnotation process). The tool only runs on the subset, and the new columns are NA for the other cells. NULL (default) annotates every cell.

log

Logger.

Value

The Seurat object with the annotation added to the metadata

Details

ident is resolved the same way the CellTypeAnnotation process resolves it: the literal "ident" means the identity column, and the column the mapping is keyed on defaults to the identity column only for cluster-based calls (a cluster-level tool, or any call given an ident). A cell-level tool with no ident stays cell-level. For celltypist with over_clustering, the mapping is keyed on the over_clustering column rather than on ident.

Calling this once per case with a different case reproduces the per-case columns of the process: EmbedSeuratCellTypeAnnotation() prefixes every new column with the case name unless add_prefix is FALSE.

Examples

# \donttest{
obj <- SeuratObject::pbmc_small
obj <- RunSeuratCellTypeAnnotation(
    obj, "direct",
    args = list(cell_types = list(g1 = "T", g2 = "B")),
    ident = "groups"
)
#> INFO    [2026-10-18 06:44:52] Running cell type annotation tool 'direct' ...
#> INFO    [2026-10-18 06:44:52] Adding annotation as new column: CellType
table(obj$CellType)
#> 
#>  T  B 
#> 44 36 
# }
